module.purpose: Renders the temporary connection line shown while a user is creating a connection between nodes, using either a custom component or one of several built-in path geometries.
module.summary: This React module connects live connection state from the flow store to an SVG overlay. It suppresses rendering when connection creation is inactive or unavailable, computes connection status styling, forwards node and handle coordinates to custom renderers, and selects Bezier, simple Bezier, step, smooth-step, or straight path generation for the default renderer.
module.businessContext: Supports visual node-editor interaction by displaying connection previews during edge creation. Failure would remove or corrupt feedback while users connect nodes.
functions: ConnectionLineWrapper (~L30-51): Gates and mounts the connection preview SVG using flow state.
ConnectionLine (~L60-122): Renders custom or built-in connection geometry from live endpoints.

detail.name: ConnectionLineWrapper
detail.signature: export function ConnectionLineWrapper<NodeType extends Node = Node>({ containerStyle, style, type, component, }: ConnectionLineWrapperProps<NodeType>)
postconditions: Returns null unless width is truthy, nodesConnectable is truthy, and inProgress is truthy.
When rendering is enabled, returns an SVG container using the supplied containerStyle and the store-provided width and height.
invariants: The SVG container has the class names react-flow__connectionline and react-flow__container.
The wrapper does not mutate application state.
edgeCases: A falsy width suppresses rendering and returns null.
A falsy nodesConnectable value suppresses rendering and returns null.
A falsy inProgress value suppresses rendering and returns null.
When all rendering conditions are truthy, the SVG width and height come from the store rather than the component props.
detail.ioFormatSpec: Returns null or a React SVG element. The rendered SVG has style={containerStyle}, width={width}, height={height}, and className="react-flow__connectionline react-flow__container".
detail.summary: Conditionally renders the connection-line SVG wrapper while a connectable interaction is in progress and layout dimensions are available. Returns null when connection-line rendering is not active.

specLiterals.role: CSS className contract for the connection-line SVG container.

specTests.then: It returns an SVG container with width 100, height 50, the supplied container style, and className "react-flow__connectionline react-flow__container".
It returns null and does not render the connection-line SVG.

units.name: ConnectionLine

detail.name: ConnectionLine
detail.signature: const ConnectionLine = <NodeType extends Node = Node>({ style, type = ConnectionLineType.Bezier, CustomComponent, isValid, }: ConnectionLineProps<NodeType>) =>
preconditions: The connection context supplied by useConnection<NodeType>() is available.
The connection context provides the coordinates, positions, nodes, handles, pointer state, and inProgress flag used by the renderer.
postconditions: When inProgress is false, the function returns no renderable output.
When CustomComponent is provided during an active connection, it is rendered with the connection geometry, metadata, style, and connection status.
When CustomComponent is absent during an active connection, a built-in connection-line path is rendered according to the selected ConnectionLineType.
invariants: The rendered connection uses the current connection context values for source and target coordinates and positions.
The configured style is passed through without modification.
The default connection-line type is ConnectionLineType.Bezier when type is omitted.
The connection status passed to a custom component is derived from isValid via getConnectionStatus.
edgeCases: When inProgress is false, the function exits without rendering a component or path.
When CustomComponent is truthy, built-in path generation is skipped and the custom component receives the connection data.
When type is omitted, Bezier geometry is selected.
When type is Step, smooth-step geometry is generated with borderRadius set to 0.
When isValid is null, the custom component receives the status produced by getConnectionStatus(null).
detail.summary: Renders the in-progress connection line using either a caller-provided component or the configured built-in path geometry. It renders nothing when no connection is currently in progress.

specLiterals.role: Default connection-line type when type is omitted.
The Step connection path is generated with borderRadius set to zero.

specTests.then: It returns no renderable output and does not render a custom component or built-in path.

specTests.when: ConnectionLine is evaluated with the current connection coordinates, positions, nodes, handles, pointer, style, type, and isValid value.
specTests.then: The custom component is rendered with those values, connectionLineType equal to type, connectionLineStyle equal to style, and connectionStatus derived from getConnectionStatus(isValid).
The built-in path uses smooth-step geometry with source and target coordinates and positions from the connection context, and borderRadius equal to 0.
